newsitem.title: USA: CoCensys says ends support for Cognex.
newsitem.headline: CoCensys says ends support for Cognex.

text.p: CoCensys Inc and the Parke-Davis unit of Warner-Lambert Co in a joint statement on Wednesday said they will phase out active detailing, marketing and patient support programs for the Alzheimer's drug Cognex, immediately.
In addition, the companies have agreed to terminate the contract for detailing the drug to U.S. neurologists.
The companies are, however, in "late-stage" negotiations for a replacement product, they said.

"Cognex has been an important milestone in the treatment of Alzheimer's disease, and our partnership with CoCensys has been an integral part of bringing the treatment to patients," said Wayne Dickerson, Director of New Business Ventures for Warner-Lambert. "We look forward to continuing our relationship with CoCensys on future projects."
He noted that Cognex remains a viable treatment option and will continue to be made available by Parke-Davis.
The companies also said they will continue to explore other co-promotion or in-licensing opportunities and are working to bring promising new drugs to market.
